title: Vagaja2023: Motor-imagery EEG during embodiment-primed MI-BCI training in VR
description: Motor-imagery EEG recorded from 26 healthy volunteers performing cued left- versus right-hand motor imagery during MI-BCI training in immersive virtual reality. Participants were split into an embodiment-primed group (virtual hand illusion) and a non-embodied control group, each completing a single run of 40 trials. The recordings also include bipolar EMG, skin temperature and accelerometry, and are re-released in BIDS format via MOABB.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 32-channel Brain Products LiveAmp using actiCAP active Ag/AgCl electrodes at 500 Hz (standard 10-20 montage), along with 2 EMG and 4 miscellaneous channels. Participants performed cue-based left/right-hand motor imagery in VR, with 20 trials per class, a 10 s imagery/feedback window and visual feedback. The study used a between-subject randomized-group design.
